## What the scanner says about `src/assets/check-icon.png`

`crimes scan --format json` returns one finding for that asset — `crime_00036`, charge **"Icon-Sized Raster"** (`raster_should_be_vector`, severity `low`, confidence `0.85`):

> "32×32 PNG icon-sized raster. SVG would scale cleanly across DPIs and ship smaller; the current asset locks the image to a single resolution."

The dimensions line in `evidence`, verbatim:

> `"dimensions: 32 × 32 px (≤ 64 threshold both sides)"`

with the two supporting lines:

> `"format: png"`
> `"consider replacing with an SVG icon — same render at every DPI, smaller bytes"`

`fix_shape` is `"ship the SVG source; rasters lose at any scale"`, `effort` is `quick`, and the suggested action is `switch_to_svg_icon`.

## Why a new SVG indicator beats another 32 × 32 PNG

**32 × 32 is the whole problem, not an incidental detail.** The detector's threshold is "≤ 64 px on both sides" — i.e. it's flagging this because at icon size the image is pure symbolic geometry (a check mark), which is exactly the case where vector loses nothing and raster gains nothing. There's no photographic detail in a 32 × 32 tick that a rasteriser needs to preserve.

**The pixels are locked to one resolution.** A 32 × 32 PNG has exactly 1,024 pixels of information. On a 2× display it's upscaled to 64 × 64 and goes soft; on a 3× phone it's 96 × 96 and visibly mushy. The usual workaround is shipping `@2x`/`@3x` variants — so copying this pattern means the new status indicator arrives as three assets to keep in sync instead of one, which is the same multiple-sources-of-truth problem the rest of this scan keeps flagging. An SVG renders sharp at every DPI from a single file.

**Bytes go the wrong way too.** A check mark or status dot as vector geometry is a handful of path commands — typically a few hundred bytes, and it gzips well because it's text. A 32 × 32 PNG carries header, palette, and compressed pixel data for a shape that could be described in one `<path>`.

**Colour and state become CSS instead of new files.** A status indicator almost certainly needs variants — green/amber/red, active/muted, maybe a hover state. In SVG that's `fill="currentColor"` and one rule. In PNG each state is another binary asset, times each DPI.

**One caveat from the same scan:** don't take "make it an SVG" to mean "wrap a PNG in SVG". `crime_00032` on `src/assets/partner-logo.svg` is the repo's only `high`-severity asset finding — "2 embedded base64 rasters inside the SVG (image/jpeg, image/png)… The SVG mime type promises infinite scale, but the actual pixels are locked to one resolution — usually larger than a plain PNG." So the new indicator should be authored as real vector paths (or re-exported from the design tool's vector source), not exported as a PNG and dropped into an `<image href="data:image/png;base64,…">` wrapper — that's strictly worse than the PNG you started with.

**Net:** the existing PNG is a `low`-severity, `quick`-effort finding — cheap to fix, and not urgent on its own. But adding a second 32 × 32 PNG next to it converts a one-file cleanup into a two-file one and bakes the DPI problem into new code. Starting the new indicator as an SVG costs nothing extra today, and leaves `check-icon.png` as the only asset to migrate later.
